samples.xml_description:
<module id="parallel2serial">
    <description>Parallel to serial converter, where every four input bits are converted to a serial one bit output (from MSB to LSB).</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operations.</input>
        <input id="rst_n">Reset signal. Defined as 0 for reset and 1 for reset signal inactive.</input>
        <input id="d" width_description="[3:0]">4-bit parallel data input.</input>
        <output id="valid_out">Valid signal indicating the availability of serial output.</output>
        <output id="dout">Serial output representing the converted data.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="COUNTER_WIDTH">Width of the counter register.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="cnt" width_description="[COUNTER_WIDTH-1:0]">Counter register.</reg>
        <reg id="valid">Valid signal register.</reg>
        <reg id="data" width_description="[3:0]">Data register.</reg>
    </logic_description>
    <implementation>
        // Assign the most significant bit of the parallel input to the serial output
        assign dout = data[3];
        
        // Sequential logic block triggered on the rising edge of the clock or active low reset
        always @(posedge clk or negedge rst_n) begin
            if (!rst_n) begin
                cnt <= 'b0;
                valid <= 1'b0;
                data <= 'b0;
            end else begin
                // Check if the counter has reached its maximum value
                if (cnt == 3) begin
                    // Update the data register with the parallel input
                    data <= d;
                    
                    // Reset the counter to zero
                    cnt <= 'b0;
                    
                    // Set the valid signal to 1 to indicate the availability of serial output
                    valid <= 1'b1;
                end else begin
                    // Increment the counter by 1
                    cnt <= cnt + 1;
                    
                    // Set the valid signal to 0 to indicate that the serial output is not yet available
                    valid <= 1'b0;
                    
                    // Shift the data register to the left by 1 bit
                    data <= {data[2:0], 1'b0};
                end
            end
        end
        
        // Assign the valid signal to the valid_out port
        assign valid_out = valid;
    </implementation>
</module>
